access.label: From Kyoto Station
access.text: Take the JR Sagano Line (San'in Line) to Kameoka Station: about 20 min by rapid, about 30 min by local train. Limited expresses (such as the Maizuru; limited express ticket required) take about 18 min.

access.label: From Osaka
access.text: Go to Kyoto Station on the JR Kyoto Line or similar, then change to the Sagano Line.

access.label: From Maizuru
access.text: The JR Limited Express Maizuru runs direct: about 1 h 10 min from Nishi-Maizuru, about 1 h 20 min from Higashi-Maizuru (via Ayabe and Sonobe).

access.label: By bus
access.text: On match days, Keihan Kyoto Kotsu runs a shuttle bus from Hankyu Katsura Station (east exit) and JR Katsuragawa Station (reserved seats, adults ¥850 one way). Check the operator's page for which matches it runs and the times.

access.label: From Kameoka Station
access.text: About 3 min on foot from the north exit. You can see the stadium from the station.

access.label: By car
access.text: The stadium car park cannot be used on match days. See “Coming by car” below for car parks you can use.

access.label: Going home
access.text: Kameoka Station gets crowded after the match. Leave plenty of time for your train or Shinkansen.

notes: On match days, the stadium car park is reserved for organisers and staff, so you cannot use it.
Roads around the stadium get busy before and after the match. Please allow plenty of time.

match_day_lots.name: SANGA CREW members' car park
match_day_lots.text: Parking tickets that only SANGA CREW (Kyoto Sanga fan club) members can buy in advance. ¥1,800 per car. Buy them on J.League Ticket by choosing “parking” for each match.

match_day_lots.name: Hozugawa River Boat Ride car park
match_day_lots.text: Right in front of the stadium's away entrance, about 1 min on foot. Open on match days only. ¥3,000 per car (cash on the day). Reservations are possible and recommended for popular matches (phone 0771-22-5846, 9:00–17:00, Japanese).

match_day_lots.name: AEON Kameoka multi-storey car park
match_day_lots.text: South of Kameoka Station. It is for shoppers. On match days and similar, special rates may apply (¥500 per 30 min, up to ¥3,000).

services.name: akippa
services.text: Book spaces at private homes and monthly car parks by the day. Opens the list around Sanga Stadium (Japanese).

services.name: Times no B
services.text: Times' reservation car parks, including Kameoka Station North Exit West, about 6 min on foot from the stadium (bookable 13 days ahead, Japanese).

services.name: toku-P
services.text: Hourly and daily reservation car parks. Search for “サンガスタジアム” after it opens to see car parks nearby (Japanese).

services.name: Nokisaki Parking
services.text: Reservation car parks. Look around Sanga Stadium on the map (some days have no listings, Japanese).

spots.name: Hozugawa River Boat Ride
spots.text: The boarding point is just east of the stadium. Wooden boats take you down the Hozukyo Gorge to Arashiyama. You can walk there from Kameoka Station.

photo.alt: A Hozugawa river boat going down the gorge in autumn

spots.name: Tamba Kameyama Castle ruins
spots.text: Ruins of the castle built by Akechi Mitsuhide. About 10 min on foot from the south exit of Kameoka Station. The ruins are on the grounds of the Oomoto religious headquarters, so follow the guidance on site.

photo.alt: Stone walls of the Tamba Kameyama Castle ruins

spots.name: Kameoka City Cultural Museum
spots.text: Exhibits on Kameoka's history and culture. About 7 min on foot from Kameoka Station. Closed on Mondays.

photo.alt: The Kameoka City Cultural Museum building

spots.name: Torokko Kameoka Station (Sagano Scenic Railway)
spots.text: Ride the open-air train along the Hozukyo Gorge to Torokko Saga. About 10 min on foot from Umahori Station, one stop on the JR Sagano Line. It does not run for part of the winter, so check the official site for operating days.

photo.alt: The Sagano Romantic Train running through the Hozukyo Gorge

spots.name: Izumo Daijingu Shrine
spots.text: The first-ranked shrine of the old Tamba Province. About 15 min by bus from Kameoka Station. Buses are infrequent, so check the timetable first.

photo.alt: The torii gate of Izumo Daijingu in cherry blossom season

spots.name: Kuwayama Shrine
spots.text: Known for autumn leaves, best in November. About 30 min on foot from Kameoka Station; there is also a community bus.

photo.alt: The main hall of Kuwayama Shrine

spots.name: Anaoji Temple
spots.text: Temple No. 21 of the Saigoku 33 Kannon Pilgrimage. Take a bus from Kameoka Station to “Anaoji-mae”.

photo.alt: The main gate of Anaoji Temple

spots.name: Yunohana Onsen
spots.text: A hot-spring village about 20 min by bus from Kameoka Station. Some inns accept day visitors for bathing (check hours and prices with each inn).

photo.alt: Yubata no Yu at Yunohana Onsen

more_spots.label: More sightseeing in Kameoka (Kameoka Tourism Association, Japanese)

match_food.name: Stadium food
match_food.text: On match days, the “Gourmet Kaido” food stalls line the outside of the stadium. From the 2026/27 season they also cover the main stand side, with 13 player collaboration dishes (each comes with an original player card). Stalls and menus change by match, so check Kyoto Sanga F.C.'s official announcements.

match_food.name: Stadium food court
match_food.text: The food court (Football Diner) on the stadium's 1st floor, with five shops including Musubiya (niku-sui beef broth and rice balls), bread, a café and beef katsu, plus a kids' area where children take their shoes off. Usually about 11:00–17:00. On match and other event days hours change, e.g. Musubiya stays open until 22:00 (each shop has its own closing days).

match_food.name: Kameoka eco Marché
match_food.text: A market held for Sanga home games at Kamekita Sanga Hiroba, the square right by the north exit of Kameoka Station. Food stalls plus local vegetables, fruit and food products. Free entry. Reusable tableware is used to cut waste. Check the dates on the organiser's page.

match_food.name: Gurukame Navi
match_food.text: Kameoka Tourism Association's food guide. Find places within 5 or 10 minutes' walk of Sanga Stadium, and filter for Kameoka beef dishes, takeout or shops with supporter offers.

specialties.name: Kameoka beef
specialties.text: Only Japanese Black cattle raised in Kameoka for 14 months or more may carry the name. Finely marbled and said to be light rather than heavy. Try it at yakiniku and sukiyaki restaurants or butcher shops.

specialties.name: Tamba sake
specialties.text: Kameoka has sake breweries, such as Tanzan Shuzo (founded 1882) in Yokomachi, within walking distance of the station's south exit, and Oishi Shuzo (Okinazuru) on the road to Yunohana Onsen.

photo.alt: Tanzan Sake Brewery in Yokomachi, Kameoka

specialties.name: Kyoto vegetables and Tamba flavours
specialties.text: Kyoto vegetables such as mizuna grow in the basin's fog and temperature swings. Tamba Dainagon azuki beans, Tamba black soybeans and autumn Tamba matsutake are local specialities.

specialties.name: Botan nabe
specialties.text: A wild boar hot pot in miso broth, served in winter at inns and restaurants in Yunohana Onsen.

specialties.name: Tawawa Asagiri (JA Kyoto farmers' market)
specialties.text: A large farmers' market with Kameoka beef, freshly picked vegetables and local products. About 13 min on foot from Umahori Station. Open 9:00–17:00.

featured_hotels.name: Hotel Route-Inn Kyoto Kameoka Ekimae
featured_hotels.text: About 1 min on foot from the north exit of Kameoka Station. Natural hot-spring bath and breakfast buffet.

featured_hotels.name: Sun Royal Hotel Kameoka Ekimae
featured_hotels.text: Right outside the north exit of Kameoka Station. Large public bath and sauna.
